title: eval-harness: per-prompt CI gating enhancements (stable thresholds + parallel runners)
author: Jordan Lee
commits_summary: 3 commits: initial implementation of per-prompt runner and gating logic; add stable-thresholds config and tests; CI pipeline glue and docs
body: Motivation: teams keep seeing intermittent prompt-set regressions that cause downstream quality flakiness. Current per-prompt CI hooks block on flaky single-run metrics and do not support parallel workers or stable thresholds, which leads to noisy failures and high developer friction. This PR introduces two complementary improvements: 1) stable-threshold gating (require N consecutive failing runs or statistical smoothing before blocking) and 2) a lightweight parallel runner to execute per-prompt evals in isolated workers to reduce wall-clock time and variance. Summary of changes: - ci/per-prompt-runner.py: new runner implementing task queue, worker pool, retry/backoff and stable-threshold logic (configurable via metrics/thresholds.yaml). - scripts/parallel_runner.sh: helper entrypoint for containerized CI agents. - metrics/thresholds.yaml: defaults for stability_count, smoothing_window, significance_delta for gating decisions. - tests/per_prompt/test_gate.py: unit and integration tests for gating logic and parallel coordination (added mocked runner and CI stub). - ci/azure-pipelines.yml: pipeline step to invoke parallel_runner with matrixed workers; improved logging and artifacts upload. - docs/ci-integration.md: documentation for configuring per-prompt gates, tuning thresholds, and interpreting results. - eval-harness/README.md: updated quickstart. Backwards compatibility: default thresholds mirror previous behavior (fail fast) unless teams opt into stable_thresholds in thresholds.yaml; we added a configuration flag enable_stable_gating=false by default to avoid surprise blocking for existing repos. Testing and validation: ran the new pipeline in staging across three prompt-sets used by marketing and search teams; observed ~60% reduction in false positives and 2.3x speedup in wall-clock CI time when using 4 workers. Metrics were captured and attached as pipeline artifacts. Rollout plan: feature gated behind per-repo thresholds.yaml; early access to power users for two weeks before turning on for all repos under the eval-harness org. Implementation notes: - The runner communicates over a small local SQLite queue to keep startup deterministic on CI agents; this avoids distributing an external queue service. - Stable gating implements an exponential moving average over the last M runs plus a consecutive-fail counter to avoid single-run spikes from blocking. - All new public config keys are documented and validated at startup to avoid silent misconfigurations. Security and performance: parallel_runner runs workers as the same CI user and does not persist secrets. CPU usage is capped per worker and defaults tuned to typical hosted CI agents. Known limitations: current implementation assumes prompt-run idempotence; we added checks to surface non-deterministic prompts in logs and will follow up with a remediation workflow. See ENG-4821 for follow-up to add stronger deduping.
review_conversation: Alex Kim: Suggest switching from local SQLite to an in-memory queue for faster throughput. Author (Jordan): SQLite chosen intentionally for CI agent restart resilience; added benchmark numbers in PR and reduced contention by using WAL mode. Priya Shah: Can we make the smoothing window configurable per-prompt-set? Author: added metrics/thresholds.yaml and validation; smoothing_window can be per-prompt-set or org default. Daniel Cortez: Requested an integration test that mimics flaky network I/O. Author: added test_flaky_network in tests/per_prompt/test_gate.py and wired it into CI. Alex Kim: LGTM after minor doc updates. Priya Shah: Approved. Daniel Cortez: Approved. CI: pipeline passed all stages on re-run after addressing review comments.
release_notes: Adds stable-threshold per-prompt gating and parallel CI runner to reduce false positives and CI latency. Backwards compatible by default; opt-in via metrics/thresholds.yaml.
